name: maybe_Field_CheckObjectState

name: maybe_Field_RegisterRailActors
summary: With the world flag at world+0x44 clear, walks the relative-offset table at self+0x314 from cursor f_354+1 to f_358; every 0x28-byte entry whose first word is >0 supplies a name pointer (entry+4, relative) that 0x0033D99C resolves, and the result is registered via maybe_Ui_RegisterActor(obj, self, 0). Then f_354 = f_358 so the same entries are not handled twice.
evidence: Both callers are themselves maybe_ names (0x001B7A38 @0.45, 0x0022742C @0.35) and pass self->f_28, so neither confirms 'field actor' nor 'rail'. The table/cursor mechanism is confirmed by the arithmetic; 'rail' is not.

name: maybe_Field_RegisterRailActors2
summary: Twin of 0x001835AC reached through a second entry: the same 0x28-byte relative-pointer loop over self+0x314 with the f_354..f_358 cursor, but Ghidra lost r4/r5 (unaff_ registers) and the entry starts with coprocessor_movefromRt (a mis-decoded VMOV). This is probably a shared tail or inline data rather than a separate routine; the '2' suffix carries no meaning.
evidence: Body is the same loop as 0x001835AC (0x0033D99C + maybe_Ui_RegisterActor) except for the lost registers; no caller, and the mangled prologue makes the entry point itself suspect.

name: maybe_Field_SpawnObjectRecordD
summary: Tail of the placement-record spawn path (the same colour-id chain 0x0066A74C/0x00628EE0/0x0063E2BC/0x0062B540 as 0x00184168): fills the actor's f_364/f_368/f_36C, applies model and sprite, copies the record's flags into f_310..f_34C and finishes with the actor sound. Ghidra lost the actor/record registers, so this is the tail of the spawn routine, not a clean 'record D'.
evidence: Body is spawn finalisation only (maybe_Model_SetupObject, maybe_Field_Actor_CreateSprite, maybe_Field_CreateActorSound) with unaff_r4/r5 standing in for actor and record; no caller. The family is right, the 'D' variant is a duplicate marker.

name: Math_RandomPercent
summary: Returns a random value in 0..99. 0x0051B1FC pulls the next value from one of the two RNG states in the game work (+0xC8 when stream==0, +0xE0 otherwise) and 0x0011CD80 is the idivmod helper; the remainder (r1) is what comes back. Nothing here counts or sizes list slots.
evidence: 0x0011CD80 is the ARM idivmod helper: 0x001BA510 reads its r1 (extraout_r1+0x78) to build a random 120..210 offset, and 0x001D5A10 uses rand%3+2 frames. Divide by 100 and return the remainder is rand()%100, so 'Ui_ItemList_GetSlotCount' was wrong.

name: maybe_Data_SelectRecordIdByWeight
summary: Random weighted pick between two record ids: draws a random float (0x0051B1FC + VectorSignedToFloat, scaled by g_0018E2A4/g_0018E2A8) and compares it with three floats read from the records named by spec[1]/spec[3] (0x00149814 lookup) to choose spec[0]/spec[3], the constant 6, or a value produced by maybe_Party_FormatStatValue.
evidence: Full 1204-byte body re-read: every branch is a random draw compared against record floats and ends in maybe_Party_FormatStatValue(id, id, flag, ...) or returns a record byte. Nothing allocates or writes text, so 'Party_BuildStatText' was wrong. What the ids mean is still open.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_ApplyModeFlags
signature: void maybe_Ui_Window_ApplyModeFlags(UiWindow* self, int mode, u32 arg3, u32 workSel)

evidence: Body only writes f_48/f_49 and returns (mode, self); 'SetInputMode' implied the mode was kept on the object, which it is not.

name: maybe_Snd_StopUiStream
summary: Fetches the game work and calls 0x005F972C on the sound-side object at work+0x10; nothing else happens. That is consistent with stopping or releasing the current UI stream, but 0x005F972C is not a decompiled entry point so the operation cannot be checked.

name: Field_Action_StartNut
summary: Starts the 'Nut' action sequence: installs the completion callback LAB_001BA5CC through owner vtable+0x84 (flushing vtable+0x88 first when immediate==0), then arms a random 120..210 frame timeout in self+0x2C when the world action flag (work+0x48+0x4C1C) is set and leaves -1 when it is not; clears f_3C and f_40.

Sibling 0x001BA5D0 uses the literal 'Nut_1' with the same FieldAction layout (self+0x28 owner, f_2C timeout, f_3C/f_40 flags); install-callback + random timeout is a start-action.

name: Field_Action_UpdateNutState

On state 8 it clears the timeout, resolves the owner's node (0x00669D54), tests for the 'Nut_1' marker via 0x00123660(...,5) and, when absent, plays the follow-up animation through maybe_Anim_PlayByNameIfPresent and pushes the two 0xFF bytes via 0x005F7F78; in the other branch it re-arms the random 120..210 frame timeout.

name: Menu_DispatchEntryAction

name: maybe_Battle_RunTargetSelection
